mechanisms.summary: Protective filters can reduce noise while also hiding weak warning signals; the UI should expose when detection is operating through a filter or shield.
A distress or anomaly signal may be cut off before interpretation completes. Preserve the partial observation instead of filling in the missing content.
A numbered or sequential marker is evidence of an observed sequence token, not by itself proof of the generator, motive, or complete sequence.
Environmental conditions can degrade a scene before assessment. Provenance should record evidence quality and loss, not silently present the surviving view as pristine.
A compact visual may be transferred as a case or task handoff. The receiving surface should preserve who supplied it, when, and what remains unverified.
A companion may remain nearby, converse in a side channel, or assist without taking over the primary task or authority lane.
Social chatter can yield visibly to investigative focus when context changes. The interface may alter animation intensity and information density without erasing the prior interaction state.

candidate_ui.anomaly_machine: baseline -> filtered sensing -> weak anomaly -> interrupted signal -> preserved partial receipt -> scoped investigation
visuals: shield/filter halo with visible attenuation state
cut-off pulse leaving an incomplete arc rather than a completed alert glyph
handoff visual carried as a provenance-tagged card or projected shard
companion channel orbit kept spatially distinct from primary work

laws: A filter may protect and still create a blind spot.
An interrupted signal remains partial evidence.
Observed sequence is not inferred causation.
Evidence quality is part of provenance.
A companion channel does not become hidden authority.
